title: ARPAPED Process Executor Protocol
description: Language-agnostic wire shape a process-kind executor (executor_kind: process, 2-RULES.md R4/R5) exchanges with the resolved Bridge, over its own connection -- one JSON object per line. Any client, in any language, reads and writes data matching these shapes; a worked example of a reference client per language lives in bridge/samples/hello_world/clients/. Distinct from schemas/bridge-protocol.schema.json, which shapes what a CONSUMER exchanges with the Bridge -- this shapes what a SPAWNED EXECUTOR exchanges with it.

invocation.description: Bridge -> process: starts one invocation. The same three inputs every executor receives, in-process or not.

output.description: process -> Bridge: a terminal successful reply, to either the original invocation or one nested call request (callRequest, below) -- the same shape either way.

error.description: process -> Bridge: a terminal failed reply, to either the original invocation or one nested call request -- the same shape either way.

callRequest.description: process -> Bridge, while handling one invocation: a nested call to another capability, resolved through this implementation's own declared dependencies.capabilities (R4) -- never a capability_id it didn't declare. Sent and awaited synchronously: a worker connection is exclusively borrowed for one invocation's whole duration, and the process never has more than one outstanding call, so the reply (an `output` or `error` message, above) can never be confused with a fresh invocation on the same connection.
